definition_zh: n. 大错；失误；vi. 犯大错；跌跌撞撞地走；盲动
definition_en: a careless or stupid mistake, or to move clumsily without seeing
core_image: 黑夜里在房间里乱撞踢翻椅子的人
scene: 他深夜摸黑走进客厅，撞翻了茶几上的花瓶。The general's blunder cost the army the whole campaign.
sceneCN: 这里 blunder 是名词「大错」（第 1 个义项：因粗心或愚钝而犯的重大失误）；句意是将军的一次重大失误葬送了整场战役。

derivatives.zh: blunder 加 -er，义为「屡犯大错的人」
blunder 加 -ing，义为「笨拙而多失误的」

senses.title: A serious careless mistake
senses.definition: a big mistake made through carelessness or stupidity
senses.definitionCN: 因粗心或愚钝而犯的重大错误
senses.example: The general's blunder cost the army the whole campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 将军的一次重大失误葬送了整场战役。
senses.why: The verb first meant to stumble blindly; a blunder is a moral stumble.
senses.whyCN: 动词本义是「盲目跌撞」，blunder 便是道德上的跌撞。

senses.title: A diplomatic or tactical error
senses.definition: an error in policy, negotiation, or strategy with wide consequences
senses.definitionCN: 政策、谈判或战略上后果严重的失误
senses.example: The treaty turned out to be a historic blunder.
senses.exampleCN: 这份条约被证明是历史性的失策。
senses.why: States stumble as people do, only on a larger floor.
senses.whyCN: 国家如人一样会跌倒，只是跌在更大的地板上。

senses.title: To move blindly and clumsily
senses.definition: to walk or grope clumsily without seeing where one is going
senses.definitionCN: 在看不见的情况下笨拙摸索前行
senses.example: They blundered through the fog toward the lights.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在浓雾中跌跌撞撞地向灯光走去。
senses.why: The original sense: stumbling in the dark, literally.
senses.whyCN: 本义即在黑暗中跌撞前行，是字面用法。

senses.title: To enter or become involved by accident
senses.definition: to get into a situation carelessly or by mistake
senses.definitionCN: 因粗心或错误而卷入某处境
senses.example: He blundered into an argument not meant for him.
senses.exampleCN: 他误打误撞地卷入了一场与己无关的争执。
senses.why: Walking blindly, one crosses doors one never chose.
senses.whyCN: 盲目行走之人，难免误入未曾选择的门。

senses.title: To say the wrong thing
senses.definition: to make an embarrassing remark by mistake
senses.definitionCN: 无意间说出令人难堪的话
senses.example: She blundered by mentioning his lost job.
senses.exampleCN: 她失言提起了他丢工作的事。
senses.why: Speech, too, has dark rooms; talk blindly and you hit the furniture.
senses.whyCN: 言语也有暗室，盲目开口便会撞上家具。

senses.title: A chess mistake losing material
senses.definition: in chess, a move that loses material or the game
senses.definitionCN: 国际象棋中损失子力或致败的错着
senses.example: A last-minute blunder gave his opponent the win.
senses.exampleCN: 最后时刻的一步大漏着让对手取胜。
senses.why: Chess adopted the word for the move a blind man might make.
senses.whyCN: 棋界借该词形容只有盲者才会走出的错着。

senses.title: To proceed stupidly despite warnings
senses.definition: to continue in error even with the danger visible
senses.definitionCN: 尽管危险明显仍继续犯错
senses.example: The council blundered ahead with the road plan.
senses.exampleCN: 议会不顾一切地推进道路计划。
senses.why: Refusing to look is itself the blindness the word names.
senses.whyCN: 拒绝去看，正是该词所指的那种「盲」。

senses.title: To grope one's way to success by luck
senses.definition: to succeed only by luck rather than judgment
senses.definitionCN: 靠运气而非判断取得成功
senses.example: The detectives blundered onto the truth at last.
senses.exampleCN: 侦探们最终误打误撞地发现了真相。
senses.why: Even blind walkers sometimes find the right door.
senses.whyCN: 盲行者偶尔也会撞对门。

intro.en: Blunder probably comes from Old Norse blunda, to shut the eyes or doze.
intro.cn: blunder 一般认为出自古诺斯语 blunda「闭眼、打盹」。

items.en: a root of drowsy, blinking dark; related forms are Scandinavian.
items.cn: 词根与「昏睡、眨眼、昏暗」相关，同族词见于斯堪的纳维亚。

items.en: blunda meant to shut the eyes, doze; blundra meant to shut one's eyes to danger.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 blunda 意为「闭眼、打盹」，blundra 意为「对危险视而不见」。

items.en: blunder first meant to stumble about blindly, then to act blindly.
items.cn: 16 世纪英格兰北部用语中，blunder 先指盲目跌撞，后指盲目行事。

items.en: the mistake sense became dominant in general and military English.
items.cn: 17 至 18 世纪，「失误」义在通用语与军事用语中占主导。

items.en: now standard for any grave careless error, including in chess.
items.cn: 今为标准词，泛指一切重大疏失，包括棋类术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the blund- sound; the near-meaning group gathers mistake words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 blund- 音；近义组收错误类词。

entries.definitionCN: 雷声——拼写相近，词源不同
碎裂——拼写相近，词源不同

normalIntro.en: Blunder began as stumbling with shut eyes, and mistakes are stumbles too.
normalIntro.cn: blunder 始于闭眼跌撞，犯错也是跌撞。

normal.en: Chess players call a losing move a blunder.
normal.cn: 棋手把致败的错着称为 blunder。

normal.en: Blunder into means to get involved by accident.
normal.cn: blunder into 指误打误撞地卷入。

normal.en: The Norse root means to shut the eyes.
normal.cn: 古诺斯语词根意为「闭眼」。

normal.en: A blunder is bigger than an error and clumsier than a slip.
normal.cn: blunder 比 error 大，比 slip 更笨拙。
blundering 可形容笨拙低效的机构。

abstract.en: See a man in a dark room kicking over every chair.
abstract.cn: 看一个人在暗室里踢翻每一把椅子。

abstract.en: Feel your hand close on the wrong door handle.
abstract.cn: 感受你的手握住错误门把的那一刻。

abstract.en: Picture a chess clock ticking as a rook slides one square too far.
abstract.cn: 想象棋钟滴答声中车多走了一格。

examples.en: The general's blunder cost the army the whole campaign.
examples.cn: 将军的一次重大失误葬送了整场战役。

examples.en: They blundered through the fog toward the lights.
examples.cn: 他们在浓雾中跌跌撞撞地向灯光走去。

examples.en: A last-minute blunder gave his opponent the win.
examples.cn: 最后时刻的一步大漏着让对手取胜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不拦的」——没人拦着他，他就在黑屋子里横冲直撞，处处闯祸。

root: 一般认为出自古诺斯语 blunda「闭眼、打盹」（更早为日耳曼词根，与昏暗、眨眼相关）；16 世纪经英格兰北部用语进入英语，先指「盲目跌撞」，后转为「犯大错」；国际象棋术语中沿用至今。

sensesIntro.en: From stumbling in the dark to stumbling in policy and chess, blunder unites blindness with mistake.
sensesIntro.cn: 从暗中的跌撞到政策与棋局的失着，blunder 把「盲」与「错」合而为一。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man kicking over chairs in a dark room
core.cn: 核心意象：暗室里踢翻椅子的人

branches.en: Grave mistakes of deed, policy, and speech
branches.cn: 行为、政策与言语的重大失误

intro.en: Blunder is a lone verb-noun pair with small derivatives.
intro.cn: blunder 是孤独的动名同形词，派生词少。

latinIntro.cn: 诺斯-日耳曼词根，无拉丁同族词。
